newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Mexico, Guatemala said undermining ACPC plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Guatemala said undermining ACPC plan.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo accused Mexico and Guatemala of undermining the export retention plan backed by Colombia and other members of the Association of Coffee Exporting Countries.

Branding the two nations "destablizing factors" in the world coffee market, Ocampo said they had increased their exports by more than 30 percent in the 1995/96 coffee year while ACPC members were cutting back on shipments in a concerted effort to boost prices.

This, in turn, has seriously limited the ACPC's possibility of success and means that Mexico and Guatemala pose a "major threat" to Colombia and other ACPC member countries, as long as they remain outside the organization, Ocampo said.
The full 14-member ACPC council accounts for more than 80 percent of world coffee production.
The ACPC agreed last May to limit green coffee exports from its members to 53.5 million 60-kg bags in the year to June 1997 against 45.8 million in the previous 12 months.

Ocampo, who spoke at the annual meeting of Colombia's National Coffee Exporters' Association, said Mexico and Guatemala had put Colombia, especially, at a serious disadvantage in the global marketplace. Their lower production costs put them in a better position to ride out any slump in world coffee prices, he said.
